_comment: Hand corrections layered over the OCR seed by tools/build_coords.py.
schematic coordinates are pixels in the matching sch<n>_full.png. The two
sheets are NOT the same size -- they were scanned about 3% apart and are
cropped separately -- so sheetImageSize carries one entry per sheet and
build_coords refuses to run if either stops matching.
This board reads far worse than A18: 47% of designators on the drawing,
against A18's much higher yield. The cause is in the artwork, not the
settings -- A17's silkscreen labels touch the component outlines, so a 'CR'
beside a diode is one connected blob with the diode body and no amount of
upscaling, thresholding or de-speckling separates them. Everything that
matters for probing is therefore placed by hand here.
_sheetRuleComment: A17 splits cleanly by number: designators below 51 are the regulator
section on sheet 1, 51 and above are the guarded digital section on sheet 2.
The exceptions are parts whose number happens to fall in the digital range
but whose circuit is on the regulator sheet -- the C65-C70 filter caps and
the two PTC thermistors R60/R61 that shunt the +/-44 S regulators.
_sheetsComment: Zone grid frames, measured from the frame lines in the full-resolution
_boardComment: Hand-placed board positions, in drawing_full pixels. 'row: true' uses the
narrower box that suits a test point in the edge row.
A test point marker goes on the PAD, not on the label: a probe sent to the
silkscreen text lands beside the hole.

marker onto the drawing and looking at it. What each one actually pointed
C55/C64, C6/TP17, C7/CR27, CR15 and CR35 both between CR34 and CR35,
F1/TP3, Q1 on the TP54-TP60 row, R1/R17, R10/R15, R19/CR19, R5 on C68,
U1 on a bare outline, U2/Q2, U5/U4, X3 on empty board.
_notOnDrawingComment: Parts with no silkscreen designator: heat sinks, insulators, spacers,
rivets, screws, nuts, ejectors, adhesive pads and the two IC sockets, which
sit under the IC they hold. They stay searchable in the parts list, but
counting them as unplaced would make the coverage badge lie.
_schematicComment: Hand-placed schematic positions, in sch<n>_full pixels. Test points are the
usual case: each is printed twice on a sheet, once in the legend table that
names its signal and once beside its flag symbol on the net, and the table
is the crisper text so the reader prefers it. A marker on a table row

_layersComment: Alignment of the photograph to board space, as four landmark pairs taken
from the edges of the PCB itself, measured in each image: the drawing's
board rectangle is x 34..5302, y 48..2947 of 5340 x 3160; the photograph's
is x 20..3360, y 75..1879 of 3400 x 1995, found by masking the blue
laminate against the bench. Both exclude the cream card-edge connector
housings, which the drawing outlines but the colour mask does not see.
Four corner pairs can only produce a scale-and-shift fit, so this is a
starting alignment rather than a finished one -- good near the middle of
the board and looser towards the corners, where the camera's perspective
shows. Add landmark pairs in Author Mode (Photo landmarks) on features away
from the edges to let it re-solve a full projective fit.
